decision: retain instruction-and-tool-contract routing with the corrected scope boundary; do not add a hook or pre-classifier

selected_system.provider_path: real Codex subscription via codex app-server

product_change.rule: Call Scout first for caller, exported API/configuration, multi-component, or broad mapping work. Start a likely single-command, single-function, or single-file task with one targeted lookup; escalate to Scout only if that lookup fails or expands the change surface.
product_change.root_cause: The previous policy treated broad lifecycle work as localized and therefore classified the MAH subscription task away from Scout even though it explicitly required every caller and exported configuration/API blast radius.

focused_routing.protocol: three broad and three local natural tasks, two repeats, stop after the first repository operation completes

initial_attempt.failure: json-version called Scout in both repeats

localized_json_version.protocol: one paired complete coding task with three behavioral checks per arm

broad_subscription_idle_timeout.protocol: one new RepoTracer run compared with the three retained baseline repeats from the same MAH-SWE task

control_surface_decision.reason: PreToolUse can block a known bad tool call but cannot safely decide semantic repository scope. A UserPromptSubmit classifier would add a model call to every prompt, and the retained Luna pre-classifier reached only 50% broad-task recall. The observed failure came from the written scope rule, not from Sol ignoring a correct rule.

limitations: The focused routing matrix measures only the first repository operation.
Three paired formal tasks are a focused release check, not a repository-wide effect estimate.
Both formal arms passed 147/151 feature checks; neither solved four sqlfmt canonicalization cases.
Formal latency favored RepoTracer on one task and baseline on two, so no latency improvement is claimed.
The interrupted 180-trial matrix remains preserved but is excluded from paired effects because subscription-account failures left no matched pairs.
The priority request path remains configurable, but prior provider logs reported actual_service_tier=default on every successful call.
